title: Remove a cassette
summary: Remove the rear wheel, counter cassette rotation with a chain whip, release the lockring and lift the cassette from the freehub.

steps.title: Work with the rear wheel removed
steps.instruction: Place the removed rear wheel securely with the cassette accessible and the rotor protected from contamination or impact.
steps.why: Cassette service is done on the wheel, not while the wheel remains clamped in the bike.
steps.warning: Keep oily tools and hands away from the brake rotor.

steps.title: Counter the freehub with a chain whip
steps.instruction: Wrap the chain whip around a suitable sprocket so the cassette cannot freewheel while you loosen the lockring.
steps.why: The freehub allows the cassette to rotate backward, so the cassette must be held while loosening.
steps.warning: Seat the chain whip fully on the sprocket teeth before applying force.

steps.title: Loosen the lockring
steps.instruction: Fully engage the lockring tool, counter the cassette with the chain whip and loosen the lockring in the normal unscrewing direction.
steps.why: The lockring retains the cassette sprockets on the freehub body.
steps.warning: Use a securely seated tool; slipping can damage the lockring or injure your hand.
steps.check: Lockring is fully loose before lifting sprockets.

steps.title: Lift the cassette from the freehub
steps.instruction: Remove the lockring, then slide the cassette or sprocket stack straight off the freehub, keeping spacers in order.
steps.why: Correct spacer order determines cassette position and indexing after reassembly.
steps.check: Cassette and any spacers are stored in their original order.
